summary:
Reed Blankenship is an NFL safety who joined the Houston Texans in 2026 after four seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles. At Middle Tennessee State, he earned first-team Conference USA honors in 2018 and 2021 and finished his college career as the team’s leading tackler in his senior season.

Philadelphia signed Blankenship as an undrafted free agent in 2022. He became a starter after an injury to C. J. Gardner-Johnson and appeared in Super Bowl LVII, which the Eagles lost. In 2023, Blankenship started 15 games and recorded 113 tackles, 11 passes defended and three interceptions. He started all 15 games in 2024, recording 78 tackles and a career-high four interceptions. He also started in the Eagles’ postseason run, which ended with a 40–22 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs in Super Bowl LIX.

On March 13, 2026, Blankenship signed a three-year, $24.75 million contract with Houston.
